transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-07 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jamal (Helios Head AI Infra), Maya (SRE), Oliver (Security), Sofia (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): deep dive into on-prem airgapped deployment. Focus on artifact delivery, offline licensing, GPU driver packaging, and runtime perf tuning (KV cache, batching, quantization).

[00:00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off, um, quick intro - Alex Carter from Redwood, and Priya is our systems engineer who will handle the deep runtime questions. Jamal, do you want to quick intro?
[00:00:14] Jamal: yeah thanks Alex, Jamal Ortiz here, head of AI infra at Helios. We run a mixture of on-prem racks, some colo, all air-gapped for production models. Primary goals are predictable latency and strong data governance.
[00:00:28] Priya: great, thanks. quick agenda: artifact delivery & manifest, offline licensing, gpu driver packaging, runtime perf knobs (kv cache, batching, quant), and bench plan. we'll leave time for q's.
[00:00:41] Maya: our main constraints: no outbound egress from prod, maintenance windows only third weekend, and we have strict change control.
[00:00:48] Alex: understood. we'll walk through options that we've done with other banks and regulated customers.

[00:01:12] Priya: starting with artifact delivery — for airgapped we provide signed tarballs containing the runtime, model artifacts, and an installer script. package includes MD5 and SHA256 manifests and a detached PGP signature. delivery methods we've used: encrypted USB, secure courier, or delivery to a staging jumpbox via partner-operated transfer. once on your side you run checksum verification.
[00:01:40] Sofia: can you clarify size? our models are ~60GB each after quantization.
[00:01:46] Priya: yes 60GB typical for a 7B variant pre-quantization; post quantization 4-bit can be ~18-22GB. runtime + deps add another ~2-4GB. we can split into chunked tarballs with a manifest to reassemble.
[00:02:03] Jamal: do you provide delta patches for future updates? don't want to retransfer big blobs every time.
[00:02:08] Priya: good question — we support incremental artifact patches, we ship patch manifests and binary diffs using xdelta for model weight deltas; still requires secure transfer but reduces size.
[00:02:20] Oliver: what about integrity and provenance — do you sign the model weights separately from the runtime?
[00:02:26] Priya: yes, separate signatures per artifact type: runtime binary, model weights, license file. we recommend verifying all three.

[00:03:00] Priya: next: offline licensing. two patterns we've used: node-locked licenses (license file per cluster with expiry) and appliance license server (a VM/appliance that is installed in the customer's network and issues short-lived tokens to nodes). node-locked is simplest but less flexible for reassignments; appliance allows central revocation and audit but adds ops overhead.
[00:03:24] Jamal: security's preference is appliance — gives us audit and ability to revoke quickly. can that appliance be fully airgapped?
[00:03:32] Alex: yes, appliance runs in the air-gapped network. licensing checks are local — nothing leaves the network. we can also support HSM-backed signing for keys if you require.
[00:03:43] Oliver: audit logs — do you produce signed audit logs for license grants?
[00:03:48] Priya: yes we can produce signed, append-only audit logs and exportable manifests for compliance review.

[00:04:12] Priya: GPU drivers and OS packages — we provide an offline driver bundle for NVIDIA drivers (we've tested 525.xx and 535.xx lines), CUDA toolkits, and cuDNN libs. note: driver compatibility depends on kernel version; we include kernel headers and a recommended kernel list.
[00:04:34] Maya: we run RHEL 8.8 with a hardened kernel. any caveats?
[00:04:38] Priya: RHEL 8.8 is fine; we'll vet driver package against your kernel. common caveat: some kernels have distro backports that require specific driver builds; we include both .run and .rpm packaging to handle that.
[00:04:52] Sofia: offline license for drivers — some vendors require separate driver licensing, right?
[00:04:56] Alex: correct, GPU vendor drivers are separate — NVIDIA's drivers are redistributable in many cases but enterprise SKUs may have different terms. we'll provide clear instructions and any vendor license artifacts to include in the package.

[00:05:30] Priya: switching to runtime perf. baseline: for non-quantized 7B model on a single A100-40GB we see ~50-80ms per token when using aggressive KV cache reuse and small-batch streaming. throughput depends heavily on batching: static batch of 8 vs dynamic batching with 200ms window leads to different p99s.
[00:05:54] Jamal: can you expand on KV cache behavior — eviction and pinning? we have multi-model traffic and want to avoid cache thrash.
[00:06:01] Priya: KV cache in our runtime keeps per-session KV shards in RAM/GPU memory. we support pinning model prefixes (hot prompts) and TTL-based eviction. for multi-tenant you can reserve a portion of GPU memory as pinned cache to avoid cross-workload eviction. mis-transcriptions: sometimes the tele transcription showed 'K V cash' — it's KV cache.
[00:06:22] Sofia: what about cold-starts — first token latency when cache not primed?
[00:06:26] Priya: cold-start will hit full attention path, so expect 2-3x latency of warm. to mitigate we recommend warmup scripts that pre-populate KV with common system prompts or use persistent sessions for long-running flows.

[00:06:55] Priya: batching: we support both dynamic batching (adaptive window up to X ms) and configured fixed batch sizes. dynamic batching is great for peak throughput but can add jitter; fixed batching gives predictable latency. our default heuristic aims for SLOs — e.g., if you target 100ms p95 we might use a 25ms dynamic window and per-route constraints.
[00:07:20] Jamal: we need p95 < 200ms for our latency-sensitive flows; for others p95 < 500ms is fine. what's recommended?
[00:07:27] Priya: for p95 < 200ms, use dedicated pools with lower batch windows (10-30ms) and enable prefix caching. also use quantized models to reduce per-token time.

[00:07:45] Priya: quantization trade-offs: 8-bit gives modest perf uplift, 4-bit can provide bigger speedups and memory reductions but may introduce quality regressions depending on model architecture and prompts. we include quantization profiles tuned per model — we've got a 'safe' int8 profile and an aggressive 4-bit LLMQ profile. we recommend running evals on your prompts.
[00:08:08] Sofia: how do quantization profiles affect KV cache size?
[00:08:11] Priya: quantized weights reduce memory footprint, so KV cache becomes a larger fraction of memory, meaning you can keep more sessions cached. however quantized execution also changes kernel selection so latency characteristics shift; you'll want to bench both.

[00:08:35] Priya: kernel selection and fusion: our runtime picks optimized kernels based on model shape and sequence length. with quantized kernels we preselect fused ops for attention to reduce kernel launch overhead. sometimes we see large wins on Ampere vs Hopper vs older gen. we'll need your exact GPU SKUs to recommend optimal kernels.

[00:09:02] Jamal: we have mix: 2x H100 and several A100s in different clusters.
[00:09:07] Priya: H100 has better tensor core perf for int8/4-bit in many ops; we'll recommend model variants per hardware. note: driver and CUDA versions can change perf significantly — we align the runtime to specific CUDA + driver combos in the artifact manifest.

[00:09:30] Alex: quick interjection on fallbacks: in Dedicated/hosted we route to nearby compatible variants if a high perf model is unavailable. in on-prem you'd configure multi-variant rollout and local fallbacks, but that requires more careful artifact ops.

[00:09:48] Maya: firewall questions — we cannot allow outbound license checks.
[00:09:51] Alex: no problem, appliance license server works entirely in your network. we support signed entitlement files for offline renewals. renewals can be done via courier or a secure partner portal transfer during approved windows.

[00:10:08] Priya: about bench plan: recommended steps — 1) customer provides exact GPU SKUs, kernel versions, and sample prompt set; 2) we'll provide artifacts and bench harness with scripts; 3) run bench in isolated window and share perf logs; 4) iterate kernel/quant profiles.

[00:10:30] Sofia: what's the harness look like? can we run it in CI?
[00:10:34] Priya: it's a set of python scripts and a C++ microbench. we include perf counters, nvprof traces, and KV cache telemetry. you can run in CI for regression checks but for isolated perf bench we recommend dedicated maintenance window.

[00:11:00] Jamal: any gotchas for memory pinning or hugepages?
[00:11:03] Priya: we support hugepages to reduce TLB pressure; we also advise GPU memory reservation for pinned KV. the installer can optionally set sysctl and hugepage configs; we provide a no-op mode for constrained environments.

[00:11:30] Priya: security notes: all artifacts are signed, installer runs as a dedicated runtime user, we support RBAC via local LDAP/SAML proxies, and audit.logs are exportable. for FIPS/HSM needs we support using your KMS to wrap keys inside the package or HSM for signing.

[00:12:02] Oliver: can we get a copy of the CIS/hardening checklist you use?
[00:12:06] Alex: yes we'll attach our hardening checklist and recommended systemd unit configs.

[00:12:30] Priya: demo of a few perf numbers — apologies, I'm reading numbers: with H100 + int8 + pinned KV we saw sustained 1200 tokens/s aggregate across a 4-GPU node at 512 context, p95 ~90ms. same node with 4-bit aggressive yields 1.9x throughput but p95 variance increases. these are ballpark and will vary by prompt.
[00:13:00] Jamal: that's promising. we need the scripts and the manifest to review with security.

[00:13:14] Priya: action items recap and who does what: we'll provide artifact checklist, MD5/SHA, driver bundle, license appliance image, hardening checklist, bench harness. Alex will follow up on licensing/pricing.

[00:13:34] Alex: next steps: I'll send an email with attached checklist and draft licensing; Priya will upload artifacts to secure portal for transfer instructions. Jamal, can you confirm SKUs by Tuesday?
[00:13:47] Jamal: yes we'll confirm. thanks all.

[00:14:00] -- End of recorded transcript (note: transcription has occasional mis-words; please rely on shared artifacts for exact manifests).
